reviews.scores: Teen on a phone: 4 before, 6 after (Atlantic 4 to 4.5, Froward 4 to 7, Dusk 4 to 7). TV viewer who watches RealLifeLore: 5 before, 7.5 after (Atlantic 5 to 6.5, Froward 5 to 8, Dusk 4.5 to 8). Motion director: 4 before, 6.5 after (Atlantic 4 to 5.5, Froward 4.5 to 7, Dusk 4 to 7). The after is clearly better on the Froward oblique and the Dusk shot. It is NOT clearly better on the Atlantic story globe, ep01's most common shot: on a phone the map reads worse than before.
weaknesses: The Atlantic story globe (clouds at 0.62) gets worse at its own job. The cloud deck is the loudest thing on the disc. At 390 px Florida is a 6-8 px orange smear lost in white noise, and Greenland, the US East Coast and the Caribbean are partly buried. ep01's clean before reads faster on a phone. For a map channel this is a step backwards on the most common shot.

The hero overlay gets softened. Florida is now a blurred orange blob with a glow halo that bleeds into the Gulf (atlantic_after_1080, about x540-590, y370-470). The antipode shot that was praised worked because its edges were crisp. Here the overlays go through bloom, depth of field and the tonemap, and they lose that crispness.

There is a visible swath seam. East of the Lesser Antilles there is a rectangular bright sheen patch with a hard, straight left edge (about x700-760, y580-720 at 1080p). On a slow push-in this is a computer-graphics giveaway a TV viewer will spot.
On the Atlantic shot the terminator looks like a dirty beige-brown filter laid over Iberia and Morocco, not golden low sun. It looks like a filter, not light.
Froward: the cloud 'clear' zone is an obvious hole in the cloud deck. The clouds fade out in an almost perfect ellipse centred on Patagonia, so it reads as a spotlight or vignette, not as weather.

Froward: the foreground clouds (5 km per pixel) are mushy blobs, and depth of field on them plus the blurred limb makes the frame edges look like a miniature. The sky above the horizon is a flat, foggy grey-blue, and the stars blurred by depth of field look like dust on the lens (top left, about x160,y45 and x390,y35).
Froward: the continental shelf around the Fuegian archipelago is a flat electric cyan, like a plastic swimming pool, with no texture. It is the most fake-looking element in the best shot.
Froward: a vertical hairline seam runs through the shelf south of Cape Froward (about x1040, y680-760). It is there in both the before and the after: a texture or patch boundary nobody fixed.
Froward: the subject marker is an unlabeled orange dot of about 20 px, which is 4 px on a phone, so it is invisible.

Dusk: the low-sun glint in the Gulf of Sidra renders as a pale salmon patch that reads as land (about x940-1060, y460-520). Italy, the one country everyone looks for in a Mediterranean shot, sits in a dead band between daylight and city lights and almost disappears.
Dusk: the night half fades into space. The planet's right edge cannot be seen and 49% of pixels are still near-black, so on a phone half the frame is black with dots.

Only stills were reviewed. Nothing has been checked in motion or after YouTube compression. Animated grain plus colour fringing on a 2x supersampled image is likely to turn into mosquito noise and banding after VP9/AVC compression. Cloud drift and depth-of-field breathing have not been checked.
Local render cost is about 7-10x ep01, and the GPU cost on the L4 is an estimate, not a measurement.
fixes: Make two presets. STORY GLOBE: clouds 0 to 0.35 at most, never over the subject continent, haze 0.2, terminator off the disc or on the limb. HERO/ESTABLISHING GLOBE: clouds 0.6, terminator on the disc. Use the hero preset for no more than about 10% of globe time (openers and transitions).

Composite hero fills, outlines and antipode shapes after bloom, depth of field and grain, or mask them out of the post pass. Keep a crisp edge plus a 4-6 px white outline, exactly as in the praised 2:40 shot.
Fix the Antilles seam in clouds_8k: fill single-pass pixels from the day before or after, or feather the sheen mask. Run a high-pass QC on the cloud map before use.

Replace the radial clear zone with density-based thinning: raise the cloud threshold locally and break the shape up with noise, so it reads as a clear-weather day over the subject, not a cut-out hole.
Exclude clouds and the limb from depth of field, don't draw (or don't blur) stars behind the atmosphere on obliques, and deepen the oblique sky toward navy.
Build the shallow-water tone control: pull the shelf toward a desaturated teal-green (about -40% saturation), modulated by seafloor texture.
Remove the meridian hairline (patch-edge alpha or wrap-UV) and add an automatic hairline/seam check to QC.

Dusk: suppress the glint when sun elevation is below about 3 degrees. Ramp city lights in across the civil-twilight band so Italy is lit. Give the night disc a faint navy earthshine or rim so the planet edge reads on a phone.
Render a 10-second motion test of each shot, encode it with the planned upload settings (1440p, CRF 14-16) and watch it on a phone before adopting. Default grain and colour fringing to nearly zero.
Measure L4 time on a 300-frame test before committing the ep02 schedule.
Adopt the renderer and post pipeline as ep02's base engine now, but do not adopt the current Atlantic settings as the default story-globe look.

reviews.scores: Teen on a phone: 3 before, 8 after. The live drain and the giant SEA LEVEL gauge are the most scroll-stopping thing in all four prototypes, though the LAND BRIDGE moment is still hard to see. TV viewer who watches RealLifeLore: 5 before, 7 after. The concept and its honesty are great, but the terrain looks like a flight simulator or video game and the foreground is blurry. Motion director: 4 before, 6 after. Right format, wrong finish: soft land texture, crumpled-foil relief, clay-like seabed, flat milky grade. The before is a decent RealLifeLore-style tilted satellite map, which is why the TV viewer scores it 5.
weaknesses: The 3x vertical exaggeration turns the Rif and Betic ranges into spiky crumpled foil or melted wax at this altitude (Morocco block of after_full, about x1100-1900, y450-900). It reads as 2005 game terrain, not Earth, and the soft 500 m land texture leaves no detail between the big peaks.

The foreground is mush. In the drained frame the bottom 40% is a smeared beige surface with stretched texels on slopes and ink-blot black holes from the baked shadows. A phone viewer sees sand, a TV viewer sees blur.

The exposed seabed looks like desert dunes or snowfields, not seabed. It is uniform tan, the white salt patches read as snow, there is no sediment variety, no accented canyons and no marked former coastline.

The hero beat at -350 m (LAND BRIDGE) is a pale sliver a few pixels wide under a leader line, with water almost touching on both sides. The label carries the claim, not the picture, and at 390 px the bridge cannot be seen.

The grade is flat and milky. Mean luma 119-143 is reached by washing everything out, not by lighting. The sky is a pale gradient with no clouds, there is no sun glint, side light does not model the water, and everything sits in the same mid-tone haze.
The water is one blue sheet with swimming-pool turquoise shallows, no surf or foam line and no depth variation in the strait. At 0 m it looks like a lake.

The UI is oversized on a TV. The STRAIT OF GIBRALTAR pill is about 40% of the frame width and covers the horizon, and the gauge plus the pill take up the whole top third. The tiny 'M' next to a 168 px number looks unbalanced.

It clashes in style with the other prototypes. It uses pill-shaped plates with an orange outline and Bebas, while the type system uses rectangular plates with an accent bar and Anton/Barlow. It also has no clouds and a different grade from CineGlobe. Cutting from CineGlobe to this would look like two different films, which is the ep01 corridor criticism again.
There are no landmarks for scale. The Rock of Gibraltar, Tangier and Ceuta cannot be identified, and there are no cities or roads.
Only 3 stills exist. The drain is the whole point (the moving waterline, the seabed reveal, shimmer on the height texture, which has no mipmaps), and none of it has been seen moving.
The ALBORAN SEA label on the leftover lake at -1,100 m is loose; that lake is the West Alboran Basin.
fixes: Drop the exaggeration to 1.5-2x, or make it depend on altitude, and say 'heights exaggerated' once in the narration. Add a 30 m DEM normal map in the hero foreground for fine relief.
Sharpen the land texture for the hero tile with a cloud-free Sentinel-2 or Landsat mosaic (for example a free 10-30 m composite), and mipmap the height texture.

Do a seabed material pass: colour by depth (sand on the shelf, grey-brown mud on the slope, dark silt in the basin), darken canyons, draw a faint former-shoreline line at 0 m, keep salt only in the last basin, and blur the baked shadows on gentle slopes to remove the blotches.
Give the land bridge its own shot. Push in on the Camarinal Sill, trace the dry crest with an orange line, add a '-287 m' callout from the data, and hold with water on both sides.

Relight: put the sun low (15-20 degrees) from a three-quarter-front angle for long shadows, add sparse cumulus and their shadows, add glint on the remaining water, deepen the sky gradient and set contrast to about 1.15. Aim for mean luma 95-120 with real dark shadows.
Shrink the labels about 30% (64 px cap, per the type system), use the type system's plate style, and keep labels beside the horizon rather than on it.
Add one or two landmark pins (Rock of Gibraltar, Tangier) for scale.
Build the globe-to-terrain match-cut and run this stage through CineGlobe's post pass (bloom, tonemap, grade), so both stages are one look.
Render a 10-15 s draft of the drain in motion at 720p and check the waterline and shimmer before making any more stills.
Re-label the -1,100 m lake 'WEST ALBORAN BASIN', or name it only in the narration. Keep every land-bridge or lake label tied to sill.py results.

reviews.scores: Teen on a phone: 2 before, 8 after. Every word reads at 390 px, and A and C are understood instantly; B's pink blob confuses. TV viewer who watches RealLifeLore: 5 before, 7 after. Clean, branded and close to RealLifeLore, but B's claim isn't visible and C's Antarctica arrow is cut off. Motion director: 3 before, 6.5 after. The size system and the QC idea are right, but it looks like a generic explainer kit, uses the same layout in every shot and still sits on the old flat globe. This is the prototype that most directly attacks the 14% mobile retention problem.
weaknesses: Shot B's graphic contradicts its own point. The 66% salmon Antarctica sits on top of the cyan Arctic Ocean, so the overlap, which is the actual claim, is hidden. The viewer sees a pink blob with cyan fringes, and on a phone it reads as 'pink Antarctica with blue bits around it'.

Shot B's headline drops 'MOST OF'. 'ANTARCTICA IS OPPOSITE THE ARCTIC OCEAN' overclaims, and the graphic itself shows the fill covering the Canadian Arctic islands and the Siberian coast. This breaks the no-false-claims rule.

Shot B: the cyan fill ends in fuzzy rounded blobs at the open-sea limits (bottom, about x1000-1350, y830-900) and looks unfinished. The orange turns salmon over Greenland and the Canadian ice, and the pole dot (about x1313, y537) is visible.

Shot A: the population dots look like grey dust or bubbles, not people. The darkened south, which is the point of the shot, can't be seen because the equator sits at the bottom of the frame. The EQUATOR plate covers dots.

Shot C: the Pacific tint barely reads; it looks like haze or glint, not 'the Pacific'. The Antarctica arrow is cut off at the bottom of the frame (a yellow stub on a phone), so the 'Americas hit Antarctica' half of the line is never shown.
All three shots use the same composition: text in the left third over navy, globe on the right. Over a 16-minute film this becomes a template, and the left 40% of every frame is empty navy space.

The look is the generic 2024 YouTube explainer kit: yellow Anton numbers, cyan and orange, a pictogram row, progress pips, heavy drop shadows. It is legible but not distinctive; nothing says 'Myth Juice'.
The fonts and plates differ from the drain and story prototypes (Anton/Barlow rectangles here, Bebas pills and quotes there), so this 'system' is not yet the film's system.

It is built on the old ep01 globe shader; the old glint smudge shows in the start frames of B and C in anim_strip. It hasn't been tested over CineGlobe clouds or bright terrain, where white text with no plate may fail.
In the mid-roll odometer frame (A, t=0.8 s) half of the '9' is clipped below the baseline. If it lingers it will look like a glitch at 30 fps.
fixes: MANDATORY before any shot like B: make the Arctic Ocean the cyan fill and Antarctica a white outline with a 35-45% fill (or outline first, fill second), so the overlap shows as a third colour. Animate Antarctica flipping over the pole onto it.
MANDATORY: put the qualifier back. Use 'MOST OF' as a kicker over ANTARCTICA / IS OPPOSITE THE / ARCTIC OCEAN, or show the share as a big number. Never drop a qualifier to save words.

Shot A: tilt the camera so the equator sits at about 60-65% of the frame height and the dimmed south is clearly visible. Make the population dots warm yellow (the colour for counted things), sized by population, and move the EQUATOR plate off the dots.
Shot C: split it into two beats (the Pacific closes; the Americas hit Antarctica) or pull the camera back. Raise the Pacific tint to a clear cyan fill of 35-40% with a crisp coastline.
Write 3-4 layout variants and rotate them: text top-centre over the sky on obliques, a bottom-left plate on bright terrain, a full-frame number card, and label-only shots.

Unify all prototypes now: one headline font (Anton or Bebas, not both), one plate style, one hero-fill opacity (55-66%), one arrow spec. Apply them to the drain gauge and labels and to the story quotes.
Add one recurring brand element, such as a signature orange accent notch or counter style, so frames are recognisable in the Suggested feed.
Test A, B and C on CineGlobe and on the drain terrain, with a 50-60% plate fallback behind text on bright backgrounds.
Ship the QC gate (fail on cap height below 48 px, more than one text block, or a headline over 4 words) and the fract() overlay-seam fix in globe.js.
Adopt now: the size floor, the palette, the T.* API and the QC gate become the ep02 standard. Fix B's graphic logic before reusing that kind of shot.

About 60% of the globe is near-black navy ocean (luma 50). On a phone it is orange slivers on a dark disc.
Bacon's arrows are thin and float in the ocean. The Africa arrow starts in open water east of Cape Agulhas instead of at the tip, and both are thinner than the type system's arrow spec.

The cut-out gives itself away. Red spill from the painting's red background fringes the ruff and the hat (after_bacon_1080, about x80-470, y330-560). The paper edge reads as a pale blue sticker outline, and a long blue stroke runs from his shoulder to the bottom of the frame (about x740-760, y700-1080). The face is noticeably softer than the type next to it.
The orange continent fills are 100% opaque, so the relief barely shows. That breaks the type system's 55-66% fill plus white outline and differs from the praised antipode style.

The Wegener standee is a bust photo with a straight horizontal crop that pretends to stand on the map. Its shadow is a dark slab beside the base, the card has no thickness, and it covers Czechia and Austria. It reads more as a sticker on Google Earth than as a pop-up book.

The paper collage with a tilt-shift miniature look is a different visual language from CineGlobe's photoreal cinematic grade. Used 10-20 times per film, it risks repeating ep01's 'style clash' criticism.
The hop arc ends at the card's top-left corner on the Czech-Austrian border, not at Graz in south-east Austria. The pop-up's first frames show a flat smear at the horizon (motion_strip, t=5.00 s).
The Bacon layout is the conventional 'portrait left, quote right' YouTube template, and the quote font (Bebas) differs from the type system's Anton.
Motion was only checked as a 12-frame strip. The squash and overshoot timing, the paper motion and the comedy beat of the hop have not been judged at 30 fps with sound.
fixes: Reframe the Bacon globe as a view from above the South Atlantic (about lat -15, alt about 2.2) so South America and Africa are both whole and their tips point down the frame. Use a brighter story-globe exposure, a 60% fill with a white outline, and thick arrows (15 px body, 63 px head) that start exactly at Cape Horn and Cape Agulhas.

Clean the matte: remove the red spill by desaturating edge pixels toward the coat colour, erode 2-3 px, then add a thin warm off-white paper edge (2-4 px, not blue) and a soft offset drop shadow. Drop the cool rim stroke.

Wegener: give the standee a fold-out paper base tab so the straight crop makes sense. Replace the slab with a short soft contact shadow plus a blurred directional shadow, shrink the card to about 35-40% of frame height, and end the arc exactly at Graz's projected point.
Start the pop-up hinge at 30-40 degrees or off-screen, and add 2 frames of motion blur or smear on the hop.

Set a budget: paper people for at most 1-2 minutes per film, only on human beats, always over the CineGlobe or terrain base, with the shared grade applied to the card, so the collage is a recurring motif and not a second world.
Use the type system's font and plates for quotes and name tags.
Render a 6-second motion test with sound effects for the hop and judge the comedy on a phone.
Template B (the Wegener standee) is close to standard after the shadow and base fixes; template A (the Bacon cut-out) needs the reframe and matte rework before it is used again.

result.summary:
1. Ep02 uses one look, "One Earth": everything happens on one photoreal Earth, built from three stages (the cinematic globe, the real terrain-and-seafloor stage and paper cut-outs of real photos), finished by one shared grade, with crisp text drawn on top afterwards. The tilted full-bleed camera fills at least 60% of the runtime, and the whole globe in black is limited to 10% of runtime and 4 s per shot.
2. Phone-first rules: must-read text at least 64 px cap height (5.9% of frame height) and nothing under 48 px (4.4%); headlines 96-120 px with at most 4 words, never dropping a qualifier like "MOST OF"; one text block plus one label; text in the top 62% of the frame; highlights at least 25 px wide on a 390 px phone; shot mean brightness at least 70 and film mean 85-130 out of 255; at most 7 s per composition; every render checked automatically for text size and as a phone-size contact sheet.
3. The plan defines 15 shot types with numeric recipes and the prototype files to reuse, a stop-doing list with ep01 timestamps, and 23 upgrades in priority order. Tier 0, about 19-27 h, comes first: separate the 3D image, the colour finish and the text into three layers in the renderer, move the type system into the production library, add the phone-check gate, adopt the new globe with STORY and HERO settings, and run motion tests. Tier 1, about 34-50 h, is mainly the terrain stage, the globe-to-terrain cut and the paper-people fixes.
4. Render cost: about 25-35 min on the Colab L4 for a 16-min film, against 15 min for ep01. This is an estimate; a 300-frame benchmark on each stage must confirm it before scheduling. Terrain data is 25-30 MB per location and stays on Drive, not on the 3.5 GB local disk.
5. Panel status: the type system is ready to adopt; the globe, drain and story prototypes need more work. Four fact or rule blockers are open: the Antarctica shot dropped "MOST OF" and its overlap graphic is wrong, the "ALBORAN SEA" label is wrong, the drain must be narrated as a thought experiment with the 3x exaggeration stated, and Wegener must land on Graz. Nothing has been checked in motion yet. The Hungarian summary is 306 words, and the combined image is 2370x6556 px and 2.05 MB with 10 labelled rows.
